summary:
EARTH TRACE is an Earth-system intelligence platform designed to investigate environmental changes, analyse long-term trends, and highlight uncertainty in satellite observations.

The platform uses NASA Earth observation and environmental datasets to explore parameters such as temperature, precipitation, vegetation and atmospheric conditions. It applies statistical techniques including the Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope estimator and Ordinary Least Squares regression to identify and quantify environmental trends.

Its unique 72-Hour Blindspot Simulator demonstrates how delayed or missing observations can affect data completeness and confidence in environmental assessments. The platform also integrates Google Gemini AI to explain complex scientific findings in understandable language.

By combining scientific analysis, interactive geospatial visualisation and AI-assisted interpretation, EARTH TRACE aims to make Earth observation data more accessible, understandable and transparent.
details:
EARTH TRACE – Detailed Project Description

1. Introduction

EARTH TRACE is an Earth-system intelligence platform developed to investigate environmental trends, explore Earth observation data and communicate uncertainty associated with incomplete observations.

It combines environmental data retrieval, statistical analysis, geospatial visualisation and AI-assisted interpretation in a single platform.

2. How It Works

Users can explore geographical locations and environmental variables through an interactive interface. The application retrieves available environmental observations, processes time-series information and presents results through maps, charts and visualisations.

The platform uses three statistical methods:

  • Mann-Kendall Test: Identifies statistically significant monotonic trends.
  • Sen's Slope Estimator: Estimates the magnitude and direction of environmental changes.
  • Ordinary Least Squares Regression: Visualises linear trends and evaluates model fit.

3. Major Features

  • Earth Explorer: Geographical exploration of environmental information.
  • 3D Earth Observatory: Interactive 3D Earth visualisation.
  • Variable Explorer: Exploration of environmental indicators.
  • Trend Detective: Statistical environmental trend analysis.
  • Global Disaster Watch: Disaster-risk information and environmental context.
  • 72-Hour Blindspot Simulator: Demonstrates the impact of missing or delayed observations.
  • AI Earth Intelligence: Gemini-powered explanations of scientific findings.
  • Reports and Analytics: Export and share investigation results.

4. Technology Stack

Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4 and React Router 7.

Backend: Node.js and Express.

Data Visualisation: Three.js, Leaflet and Recharts.

Artificial Intelligence: Google Gemini API and Google GenAI SDK.

Authentication: Firebase Authentication.

5. NASA Data and Scientific Resources

NASA POWER provides meteorological and environmental observations used in the application.

NASA MERRA-2 provides atmospheric reanalysis context.

Other resources and datasets are used for disaster-risk information, environmental analysis and visualisation.

6. Innovation

The major innovation is the integration of statistical trend detection with an observation-gap simulation.

The 72-Hour Blindspot Simulator demonstrates how incomplete observations can affect confidence in environmental assessments and encourages users to consider uncertainty before drawing conclusions.

7. Expected Impact

EARTH TRACE aims to support environmental education, research, data exploration and better-informed environmental assessments by making scientific information more accessible and understandable.

8. Future Scope

Future development includes real-time observation-quality monitoring, additional validated environmental datasets, enhanced geospatial analysis, improved disaster-data integrations and more advanced uncertainty assessment.
